**Neilia Hunter Biden** (née **Hunter** ; July 28, 1942 – December 18, 1972) was an American teacher. Biden was also the first wife of [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden"), who later became the 46th [president of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States"). She died in a car crash with their one-year-old daughter, Naomi; their two sons, [Beau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beau_Biden "Beau Biden") and [Hunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunter_Biden "Hunter Biden"), were injured but survived the incident. Her death occurred six weeks after her husband's [election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_United_States_Senate_election_in_Delaware "1972 United States Senate election in Delaware") to the U.S. Senate.
## Early life and career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Neilia_Hunter_Biden&veaction=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and career") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Neilia_Hunter_Biden&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section's source code: Early life and career")]
Neilia Hunter was born on July 28, 1942, in [Skaneateles, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skaneateles,_New_York "Skaneateles, New York"), to Louise (née Basel) and Robert Hunter, who were Presbyterians.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-NHJBNJ-2) Neilia had two brothers, John and Michael.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-3) She attended Penn Hall, a [secondary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secondary_school "Secondary school") boarding school in [Chambersburg, Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chambersburg,_Pennsylvania "Chambersburg, Pennsylvania"). She was active in the school's [French club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language"), [field hockey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_hockey "Field hockey"), [swimming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_\(sport\) "Swimming \(sport\)") and [student council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Student_council "Student council").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-JBM6Y-4) After secondary school, she attended [Syracuse University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse_University "Syracuse University") and was a school teacher in the [Syracuse City School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse_City_School_District "Syracuse City School District").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-NHJBNJ-2)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-The_One_D.O.-5) She was an English teacher at the Bellevue School in [Syracuse, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse,_New_York "Syracuse, New York").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-The_One_D.O.-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-buffalonews-6) She was a first cousin of former [Auburn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auburn,_New_York "Auburn, New York") city councilman Robert Hunter.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-7)
## Personal life
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Neilia_Hunter_Biden&veaction=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Personal life") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Neilia_Hunter_Biden&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section's source code: Personal life")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/14/Neilia_Hunter%2C_Joe%2C_Hunter%2C_Naomi_Christina%2C_and_Beau_Biden%2C_c._1972_%28removed_text%29.jpg/250px-Neilia_Hunter%2C_Joe%2C_Hunter%2C_Naomi_Christina%2C_and_Beau_Biden%2C_c._1972_%28removed_text%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Neilia_Hunter,_Joe,_Hunter,_Naomi_Christina,_and_Beau_Biden,_c._1972_\(removed_text\).jpg)The Biden family c. 1972, (clockwise from top left): Neilia, Joe, Hunter, Beau, Naomi
Neilia Hunter met [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden") in [Nassau, Bahamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nassau,_Bahamas "Nassau, Bahamas").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-OEJBNYR-8) Shortly afterwards, Biden moved to Syracuse to be closer to her and attend law school.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-The_One_D.O.-5) The couple married on August 27, 1966.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-JBM6Y-4) After Biden graduated from law school, the couple moved to [Wilmington, Delaware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilmington,_Delaware "Wilmington, Delaware"), where he was on the [New Castle County Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Castle_County_Council "New Castle County Council"). They had three children: [Joseph Robinette "Beau" III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beau_Biden "Beau Biden"), [Robert Hunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunter_Biden "Hunter Biden") and Naomi Christina ("Amy").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-9) While Biden was campaigning to unseat U.S. Delaware senator [J. Caleb Boggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Caleb_Boggs "J. Caleb Boggs"), Neilia was described by _[The News Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_News_Journal "The News Journal")_ as the "brains" of his campaign.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-JBM6Y-4)
## Death
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Neilia_Hunter_Biden&veaction=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Death") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Neilia_Hunter_Biden&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section's source code: Death")]
On December 18, 1972, shortly after Joe became U.S. senator-elect, Neilia was driving with her three children west along rural Valley Road in [Hockessin, Delaware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hockessin,_Delaware "Hockessin, Delaware"). At the intersection with [Delaware Route 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delaware_Route_7 "Delaware Route 7") (Limestone Road), their vehicle pulled out in front of a [tractor-trailer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tractor-trailer "Tractor-trailer") truck traveling north along Route 7 and was struck by it. Police determined that Neilia had driven into the path of the tractor-trailer.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-biography-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-11) The truck driver, identified as Curtis C. Dunn, aged 47, of [Avondale, Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avondale,_Pennsylvania "Avondale, Pennsylvania"), escaped without any major injury (he died in 1999).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-13) All four occupants of Biden’s vehicle were taken to [Wilmington General Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilmington_General_Hospital "Wilmington General Hospital"), where Neilia and Naomi were pronounced dead on arrival. Three-year-old Beau and two-year-old Hunter were treated for non-life-threatening injuries, Beau with a broken leg and other wounds, and Hunter with a minor skull fracture and other head injuries.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-14) Two weeks after the crash, Joe was sworn into the [Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Senate_career_of_Joe_Biden "US Senate career of Joe Biden") at the hospital where his two sons were being treated.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-JBM6Y-4) Neilia and Naomi were buried in [St. Joseph on the Brandywine Cemetery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph_on_the_Brandywine "St. Joseph on the Brandywine") in [Greenville, Delaware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenville,_Delaware "Greenville, Delaware").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-15)
## Legacy
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Neilia_Hunter_Biden&veaction=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Legacy") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Neilia_Hunter_Biden&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section's source code: Legacy")]
In a commencement speech at [Yale University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale_University "Yale University") in 2015, Joe Biden, then serving as [U.S. vice president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Vice_President "U.S. Vice President") under President [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama"), spoke of his wife. He said "The incredible bond I have with my children is the gift I'm not sure I would have had, had I not been through what I went through [after the fatal crash]. But by focusing on my sons, I found my redemption."[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-16)
Dedicated in her memory, Neilia Hunter Biden Park is in a suburban area of unincorporated [New Castle County, Delaware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Castle_County,_Delaware "New Castle County, Delaware").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-17) [Cayuga Community College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cayuga_Community_College "Cayuga Community College") in Auburn, New York, where Neilia's father ran the food service operation for many years, annually confers the Neilia Hunter Biden Award on two graduates—one is conferred for [journalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Journalism "Journalism") and the other for [English literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_literature "English literature").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-18) Among the early winners was [William "Bill" Fulton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Fulton_\(urban_planner\) "William Fulton \(urban planner\)"), who later served as mayor of [Ventura, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventura,_California "Ventura, California").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-19) A memorial plaque was erected at Bellevue Elementary School in Syracuse in Neilia's memory.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neilia_Hunter_Biden#cite_note-buffalonews-6)
